title: The Devout Woman and the Two Wicked Elders (मराठी)

keywords: the devout woman and the two wicked elders
full_text:
In an ancient city lived a noble and devout woman named Sarah, whose beauty of character, modesty, and devotion to charity were revered by all the citizens. Two elderly judges of the high court, whose hearts were secretly corrupt, sought to force her to compromise her honor. When Sarah rejected their corrupt advances with righteous indignation, the wicked elders conspired to destroy her.

They appeared before the King’s supreme council, tearing their robes and claiming they had witnessed Sarah violating the sacred laws of the realm in her garden. Because the accusers were venerable judges with long white beards, the king and the populace believed their testimony, and the innocent woman was condemned to be cast from the city precipice.

As the guards led Sarah through the public square, a clever young youth named Daniel stepped forward and shouted to the crowd: 'Hold your hands! Will you shed innocent blood upon the word of two corrupt witnesses without testing their testimony?'

The king, observing the youth’s extraordinary confidence, halted the procession: 'How would you test them, young man?'

Daniel said: 'Separate the two judges so that neither can hear the other speak, and let me examine them one by one.'

The judges were led to opposite sides of the square. Daniel approached the first elder and asked: 'You swore you saw this deed committed in her garden. Tell the court: beneath which tree did it take place?'

The first elder answered without hesitation: 'Beneath the spreading boughs of the great mastic tree!'

Daniel recorded the answer, walked across the square to the second elder, and asked: 'Under which tree in the garden did you witness this deed?'

The second elder replied confidently: 'Beneath the tall, leafy green oak tree!'

Daniel turned to the King and the crowd: 'Behold the falsehood of their conspiracy! One claims a mastic tree, and the other an oak! Their own tongues have exposed the web of their deceit!'

The crowd cheered in triumph for the truth. The king exonerated the virtuous Sarah with royal honors, stripped the corrupt elders of their robes, and appointed young Daniel to his council of justice, demonstrating that the light of truth pierces the darkest deceptions.
moral: Innocence is protected by truth, and corrupt judges will be exposed by the sharp light of inquiry. [MR]
